references_experience.text: Human Services Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) 1. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number OMAS-FDA-NCTR-2026-132591 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Pristima® Pre-Clinical Data Management System Maintenance and Support. This acquisition is not set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at Acquisition.gov. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), National Center for Toxicological Research (NCTR), intends to issue a Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order on a sole-source basis to Xybion Corporation: Xybion Corporation UEI: REENR8LT12K3 2000 Lenox Drive, Suite 101 Lawrenceville, NJ 08648-2314 The Government's decision to restrict competition is supported by an approved Sole Source Justification prepared pursuant to FAR 12.102(b) and FAR 12.201-1. 2. certifications_partner.text: tinued commercial maintenance and support services for the Government's existing Pristima® Pre-Clinical Data Management System. The requirement includes manufacturer-authorized: Software maintenance; Technical support; Installation assistance; Software updates; Software upgrades; and Vulnerability patches necessary to maintain the Government's existing Pristima® implementation. Xybion Corporation is the proprietary developer and manufacturer of the Pristima® Pre-Clinical Data Management System. Market research confirmed that Xybion Corporation is the exclusive provider of the required manufacturer-authorized maintenance and support. This would include: International Standards Organization (ISO) processes, organization charts, briefings, and data that organizations put in shared organization drives. 1.6 Content-ID Content-ID is a way to categorize a related set of activity data, for example: “Digital Nautical Charts” or “Absolute Gravity Survey.” A Content-ID is a unique identifier created when a logical set of activity data is registered in the ATLAS’s Data Inventory. Each data set identified by a Con- tent-ID has a DC and Data Steward (DS), retention/lifecycle policies, and access control policies. The Content-ID is used to track data throughout the migration process. Virtual folders within S3 buckets are created based on Content-ID, and access control and lifecycle policies are then applied to those Content-ID virtual folders based on the rules for that logical set of data. 1.7 Roles Data is acquired, managed and provisioned through various user roles, as identified in Table 3. This process applies to moving data to the ODS, establishing storage in the ODS with the appropriate accesses, and creating data feeds. Each data set may have unique issues and considerations. ODS cloud mi- gration preconditions are: 1. A Data Custodian must be identified, 2. Data must be registered in the data inventory such that a ContentID is associated with the data, and 3. Essential metadata (a minimum set) must be populated for the particular data set. This process is the same for both file/object based data and database data with a few exceptions: 1) database data will not be posted to a dirty bucket, but instead to its designated database struc- ture, and 2) while the ISP and DSP will move database data, as they move file/object data; it will be up to the ASP to ETL data into the cloud’s database. 3.2.1.1 Phase 1: Identify Content The identity phase begins when a party (CDO, DC, DS, or PM) identifies data to be migrat

If the Government POC determines that the outage restoration time frames cannot be met for other non-mission essential functions, the Government POC can declare any outage restoration priority level as high to medium to low if the outage significantly affects the mission of the Government. 2.1.4.1. High Priority Outage 2.1.4.1.1. A high priority outage is normally a sudden and widespread disaster stemming from the result of a man-made or natural disaster in which property, equipment, and site infrastructure are destroyed. The Contractor shall respond onsite to the outage NLT one hour of receipt of notification by the CFP or Government POC and advise the CFP and Government POC of its restoration procedures for a catastrophic situation. The Contractor shall provide the CFP or Government POC with updates NLT every four-hours on the status of restoration actions. 2.1.4.1.2. The following defines a high priority outage: • Loss or degradation to any single or multiple Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) and Primary Rate Interface trunk(s), to include supporting systems infrastructure (Core Unified Communication Servers/ Database/ SAN), supporting wireline/fiber infrastructure, and delivery sys

ge when the Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR) falls below 25% of system capacity - Partial loss of SIP /PRI Trunking capability to the Government facility regardless of the source location of the outage when the Dropped Call Rate (DCR) exceeds 50% of system capacity - Loss of greater than 75% of total call handling capability of any legacy analog communications system 2.1.4.2. Medium Priority Outage 2.1.4.2.1. A medium priority outage may be a sudden or widespread disaster stemming from the result of a man-made or natural disaster, which disrupts service to property, equipment, and site infrastructure. The Contractor shall respond on-site PWS-Version 12 Dated: 14 April 2026 Robins AFB, GA Page 6 of 21 to the outage NLT 24-hours after receiving notification by the Government POC and CFP. 2.1.4.2.2. The following defines a medium priority outage: • Loss or degradation to any single or multiple SIP/PRI trunk(s), to include supporting systems infrastructure (Core Unified Communication Servers/ Database/ SAN), supporting wireline/fiber infrastructure, and delivery systems (i.e. MPLS or equivalent) regardless of location, that result in the following conditions: - Partial loss of SIP /PRI Trunking capability to the Government facility regardless of the source locat

of SIP /PRI Trunking capability to the Government facility regardless of the source location of the outage when the CSSR falls below 75% of system capacity - Partial loss of SIP /PRI Trunking capability to the Government facility regardless of the source location of the outage when the DCR is greater than 5% but less than 50% of system capacity - Loss of greater than 25% but less than 75% of total call handling capability of any legacy analog communications system 2.1.4.3. Low Priority Outage 2.1.4.3.1. A low priority outage minimally disrupts service to property, equipment, and site infrastructure. The Contractor shall respond on-site NLT five working days of notification by the Government POC and CFP. All future references to days shall indicate working days unless otherwise noted. 2.1.4.3.2. Under this CSO, the DoD may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches, and/or proposals from traditional and nontraditional business entities for innovative commercial products, technologies, and services, or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial products, technologies, and services to meet U.S. Army needs and improve readiness. These include, but are not limited to, IT modernization, enhanced cybersecurity, efficient artifact restoration and conservation, streamlined base operations, and improved facility support. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include, but are not limited to, commercially-available products, technologies, or services immediately available; commercially-available products, technologies, or services fueled by commercial or strategic investment; and concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial products, technologies, or services, existing Government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. The G

ars have been reserved for awards under this CSO. The participating DoD agencies will provide no funding for direct reimbursement of white paper or proposal development costs. NOTE: During any step of the CSO, the Government may send written questions or comments for companies to address via email, or other suitable communication methods as determined by the Government. Benefits of the CSO process and the potential for award include: A streamlined application process requiring only minimal corporate and technical information for fast-track evaluation timelines for solution briefs. Negotiable payment terms for non-dilutive capital. Negotiable intellectual property (IP) rights. Secure and direct feedback from end users, mission partners, and users within the DoD to help product teams develop and hone product design and functionality. Each proposal is evaluated on its individual merits rather than on a comparative basis. sla_onsite.text: ionally situated within the Office of the Deputy Under Secretary for Health for Clinical Services. VHA FSO is partnering with the Office of Rural Health (ORH) to expand food locker programing, to be known as NouRISH (Nutrition, Resources, and Integrated Support for Health). FSO is advancing a West Palm Beach proof of concept to expand food locker programming across rural and highly rural sites. The Enterprise-Wide Initiative (EWI) uses an interdisciplinary framework designed to connect Veterans with reliable food resources and comprehensive wraparound services that address health related social needs. Food lockers are secure food distribution sites for Veterans who are experiencing food insecurity so that they may access healthy food, especially for Veterans who cannot reach traditional food pantries during limited hours or who face transportation, stigma, or scheduling barriers. Veterans enrolled in the Food Locker Program have been screened positive for food insecurity and have diet related diseases. The Veterans will be given a “prescription” for medically tailored groceries to be placed in a locker providing accessibility to the Veteran in a dignified, convenient manner. The lockers will properly store perishable and non-perishable items for Veterans that are food insecure and/or

excesses in the diet. The most addressed conditions in nutrition programming include diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease (CVD). SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor shall furnish, deliver and install the food lockers and provide required software, warranty and maintenance for operational function to VA Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOC) or other VA owned facilities. The contractor must furnish all materials, transportation, and expertise necessary to provide a properly installed and functioning smart locker food system. The contractor shall consult with the site point of contact to assess the readiness of the proposed installation site to ensure safety and accessibility, including verification of adequate electrical outlets. Delivery and site specifications will be established at the order level. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS: The following supplies are required: Single point connection of a 220 Volt Single Phase (4) wire circuit for each terminal. Dual temperature control lockers (the ability to freeze and refrigerate). Large lockers - Approximately 12 large lockers (each locker shall measure approximately 16”W x 18”L x 18”D). Small Lockers – Approximately 6 lockers each locker shall measure approximately 16”W x 18”L x 18”D). Kiosk must have a touchscreen. Cellular connection c

pproved designed logo. User authentication; A single, reusable ID or PIN per participant. Complies with American with Disabilities Act (ADA) easy and secure access Meets National Sanitation Foundation standards to ensure sanitary and safe storage. Initial Set-Up and Maintenance Initial setup shall include delivery, installation, and education for VA staff on proper equipment use. The contractor must coordinate all delivery arrangements with point of contact at each facility and protect all items from damage during shipping. All repairs must be performed by the contractor or contractor approved personnel within one week. Warranty must include onsite and/or online repairs and over-the-phone and/or online support. The contractor must maintain units and make repairs throughout the period of performance. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The period of performance shall be five years from the date of the award of the Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA).
